notes.decision: Running header 'Of the Teacher' — ⲡⲥⲁϩ (Lycopolitan ⲡⲥⲁⲍ) = 'the Teacher,' the standard designation for Mani throughout the Kephalaia.
'The First Father' — translation of the Manichaean technical term for the Father of Greatness, the supreme deity of the Realm of Light.
'The first Power.' ⲟⲁⲙ is the Lycopolitan/Sub-Achmimic form of Sahidic ϭⲟⲙ ('power, might'). Used as a technical term for an emanated cosmic Power.
'Great' — Lycopolitan ⲛⲁⲟ = Sahidic ⲛⲟϭ. Throughout this page ⲛⲁⲟ functions as the standard adjective 'great.'
'The first eternal one' — ϣⲁ ⲁⲛⲏϩⲉ ('unto eternity') used as substantive epithet of the First Father. Lit. 'the first of/who-is-unto-eternity.'
'The root of all the lights.' ⲛⲟⲩⲛⲉ = root; the First Father is the radical source of all luminous emanations.
'The three emanations.' ⲡⲣⲟⲃⲟⲗⲏ (Greek προβολή) is the standard Manichaean term for an emanated divine being; rendered 'emanation' per preferred terminology.
'They humbled the Darkness.' ⲫⲃⲓⲟ = 'to lower, humble, abase' (Sahidic ⲑⲃⲃⲓⲟ). Capitalizing 'Darkness' as it functions here as the cosmic principle/realm.

'His depth of heart' — literal rendering of the idiom ⲱⲕ ⲛϩⲏⲧ (lit. 'extension/length of heart'), which in this context describes the Darkness's deep-rooted obstinacy or arrogance. Kept literal to preserve the spatial image; cf. line 17 ⲡⲱⲕ ⲛϩⲏⲧ ⲛⲧⲙⲛⲧⲛⲁⲟ ('the depth of heart of greatness') applied positively to the Realm of Light.
'They crushed' — ⲟⲩⲱϣϥ = to break, smash, crush. Preserves the physical violence of the verb.
'They appointed a king for themselves alone.' ⲡⲟⲣⲟ = Lycopolitan form of ⲡⲣ̄ⲣⲟ ('the king'). ⲛⲉⲩ ⲟⲩⲁⲉⲧⲟⲩ = 'to themselves alone.'
'For the eons' — Greek loanword αἰῶνες, the cosmic ages/realms. Kept as 'eons' to preserve the Manichaean technical sense (the Aeons of Light).
'The Third Ambassador' — Greek πρεσβευτής ('envoy, ambassador'), standard Manichaean title for the Third Messenger.

'The fore-image.' Greek προτομή literally = 'fore-cut, foremost part, bust.' Used here for a representational front-form of the King of Lights. Distinguished deliberately from ⲡⲣⲟⲃⲟⲗⲏ (emanation) and ⲡⲉⲓⲛⲉ (likeness); 'fore-image' preserves the προ- ('forward, foremost') element of the compound.
'He called and sent forth.' ⲧⲱϩⲙⲉ = 'to call, summon' (Sahidic ⲧⲱϩⲙ); ⲧⲛ̄ⲛⲁⲩ ⲁⲃⲁⲗ = 'to send out' (Sahidic ⲧⲛⲛⲟⲟⲩ ⲉⲃⲟⲗ). ⲁⲃⲁⲗ here preserves outward direction.
'The Pillar of Glory' — Greek στῦλος + ⲡⲉⲁⲩ ('the glory'); the standard Manichaean technical name for this divine Power.
'The Perfect Man.' ⲭⲏⲕ ⲁⲃⲁⲗ = 'completed, perfected' (lit. 'finished out'). Standard Manichaean title.

'The one who lifts up beneath all things.' ⲧⲃⲓ here = Sahidic ϥⲓ ('to lift, bear, carry'). ⲁϩⲣⲏⲓ̈ ϩⲁ preserves directional 'up under' — the Pillar of Glory bears the cosmos from beneath. Translating consistently as 'lift' for both occurrences (cf. L16).
'Praise' — ⲥⲙⲟⲩ/ⲥⲙⲁⲙⲉ = 'to bless, praise.' Hence 'Pillar of praise' parallel to 'Pillar of glory.'

'The great Omophoros who carries all the omophoroi.' ⲱⲙⲟⲫⲟⲣⲟⲥ = Greek ὠμοφόρος ('shoulder-bearer'); kept untranslated as it is the established Manichaean title for the cosmic supporter. ⲛⲉⲉϥ = 'to carry, support.'

'Jesus the Radiant who is glorified.' ⲡⲡⲣⲓⲉ derives from ⲡⲣⲓⲱ ('to shine, dawn') — the verbal-active form. Rendering as 'Radiant' rather than the static 'Splendor' preserves the actively-shining quality of the Coptic root, faithful to the correspondential principle that light corresponds to active emission, not to a quality observed from outside.
'The one through whom they give eternal Life.' ϩⲓⲧⲟⲟⲧϥ = 'through his hand/agency'; ⲡⲱⲛⲉ̄ ϣⲁⲁⲛⲏϩⲉ = 'the life unto eternity.'
'The Virgin of Light, the Wisdom.' Both Greek loanwords (παρθένος, σοφία). Manichaean technical title for the third Power called by the Third Ambassador.

'Who lifts away the heart of the [arch]ons and Powers.' Editor-restored [ⲁⲣⲭ]ⲱⲛ confirmed by Manichaean cosmological context: the Virgin of Light's seductive role with the male and female archons. Maintaining 'lift' for ⲧⲃⲓ for consistency with L11.

notes.coptic_form: ϩⲛ̄ ⲧⲉⲥϩⲓⲕⲱⲛ ⲉⲥⲭⲱⲕ ⲁⲃⲁⲗ ⲙⲡⲱⲕ ⲛϩ[ⲏ]ⲧ ⲛⲧⲙⲛⲧⲛⲁⲟ
notes.decision: 'In her image (icon), perfecting the depth of heart of greatness.' ϩⲓⲕⲱⲛ = εἰκών. ⲡⲱⲕ ⲛϩⲏⲧ here echoes the same idiom from L5 but inverted to a positive cosmic register — the deep interior of the Realm of Greatness. Literal preservation of the spatial idiom.
'The Third Father ... is Jesus the Radiant.' The text identifies the Third Father with one of the Powers called by the Second Father — Jesus the Radiant — establishing the descending chain of triads.

'Three callings according to the likeness of the Second Father.' ⲡⲉⲓⲛⲉ rendered as 'likeness' per mandatory terminology; the structure of three Powers parallels (is in the likeness of) the Second Father's pattern.
'The Mind of Light.' ⲛⲟⲩⲥ (νοῦς) translated as 'mind' per mandatory terminology. The Light Mind is the first of Jesus the Radiant's three callings.

notes.coptic_form: ⲡⲉⲧⲁ ⲓⲏⲥ ⲕⲁⲁϥ ⲁϩⲣⲛ̄ ⲡⲉⲛⲉⲓⲛⲉ ϩⲛ̄ ⲧⲉⲕⲕⲗⲏⲥⲓⲁ ⲉⲧⲟⲩⲁⲃⲉ
notes.decision: 'Whom Jesus established before our likeness in the holy church.' ⲕⲁⲁϥ ⲁϩⲣⲛ̄ = 'set him before/at the mouth of'; ⲡⲉⲛⲉⲓⲛⲉ rendered 'our likeness' per mandatory terminology — the Light Mind stands as archetype before the human community.

notes.coptic_form: ⲡⲛⲁ[ⲟ ⲛ̄ⲕⲣⲓ]ⲧⲏⲥ ⲉⲧϯϩⲉⲡ ⲁⲛϯⲩⲭⲁⲩⲉ ⲧⲏⲣⲟⲩ ⲛ̄ⲛ̄ⲣⲱⲙⲉ
notes.decision: 'The great [Ju]dge who gives judgement upon all the souls of men.' Editor-restored [ⲕⲣⲓ]ⲧⲏⲥ (κριτής) confirmed by ϯϩⲉⲡ ('to judge'). ⲛϯⲩⲭⲁⲩⲉ = ⲛⲯⲩⲭⲁⲩⲉ ('the souls,' ψυχαί).

notes.coptic_form: ⲉⲣⲉ ⲧⲉϥⲥⲕⲏⲛⲏ ⲥⲙⲁⲁⲛⲧ̄ ϩⲛ̄ ⲡⲁⲏⲣ ϩⲁ ... ⲧⲣⲟⲭⲟⲥ . [. .]ⲥⲓⲟⲩ
notes.decision: 'With his tabernacle established in the air beneath [...] the wheel [of the st]ars.' Restoration [ⲛⲥ]ⲓⲟⲩ ('of the stars') is highly probable from ⲧⲣⲟⲭⲟⲥ ('wheel') context — the cosmic wheel of stars is a standard Manichaean structure. ⲥⲕⲏⲛⲏ = 'tabernacle, tent.'
'The Third Power is the Youth, the great [...].' ⲗⲓⲗⲟⲩ = 'youth, child' (Lycopolitan). Likely the Manichaean figure of the Light-Youth/Maiden, but the immediate epithets are damaged.
'Light in his face, two/twice in [...].' ⲡⲣⲟⲥⲱⲡⲟⲛ = πρόσωπον. ⲥⲛⲉⲩ = 'two' or 'second.' Lacuna prevents determining whether '(a) second' or 'twofold' is meant.

notes.coptic_form: ⲉⲓ̈ⲥⲉⲭⲉ ⲁⲧⲡⲏ ⲉⲧⲁϥⲥⲙⲛⲧϥ ϩⲙ ⲡⲧⲱϩⲙⲉ [ⲙⲛ] ⲡⲥⲱⲧⲙⲉ
notes.decision: '[He is] held on high, whom he established through the calling [and] the hearing.' ⲉⲓ̈ⲥⲉⲭⲉ is unclear — possibly Greek ἔχω-stem ('held'); ⲁⲧⲡⲏ = 'on high' (ⲡⲏ = ⲡⲉ 'heaven' in Lycopolitan). The pair ⲧⲱϩⲙⲉ/ⲥⲱⲧⲙⲉ = 'call/hearing' is the Manichaean dyad of summons and response.

'[He stood] himself beside his [Father].' ⲧⲱⲕ ⲁⲣⲉⲧ⸗ = Lycopolitan equivalent of Sahidic ⲱϩⲉ ⲉⲣⲁⲧ⸗ ('to stand upright'). Editor's restoration accepted; ⲡϥⲓⲱⲧ = 'his Father' completes the line by parallel with L32.

'[The] King of [...] of the s[on?]....' ⲡⲥⲏⲣ is uncertain — possibly an unusual orthography for ⲡϣⲏⲣⲉ ('the son'), but ⲥ for ϣ is irregular even in Lycopolitan. Could alternatively represent another root. Left unrestored.

notes.coptic_form: ⲛⲉⲩ ⲁⲣⲁϥ ⲉϥⲭⲱ ⲙⲙⲁⲥ ... [ⲁ]ⲛⲁⲕ ⲡⲉⲧⲁⲓ̈ⲛⲉⲩ ⲁⲣⲁϥ ϩⲁⲧ�m ⲡⲁⲓ̈ⲱⲗⲧ
notes.decision: '(They?) saw him saying [...] I am the one whom I have seen beside my Father.' Direct discourse formula. The pattern 'what I see beside my Father, that I do' is a Manichaean adaptation of John 5:19, here applied to the Youth (the third Power of Jesus the Radiant).

notes.coptic_form: [ⲡⲉϯⲭⲱ ⲙⲙⲁϥ ⲛ̄ⲧ]ⲱⲧⲛⲉ ϩⲱⲧⲧⲏⲛⲉ ⲡⲉⲧⲁⲧⲉⲧⲛ̄ⲛⲉⲩ ⲁ[ⲣⲁϥ ϩⲁⲧⲙ̄ ⲡⲉⲧⲛⲓ̈ⲱ]ⲧ ⲡⲉⲧⲉⲧⲛ̄ⲉⲓⲣⲉ ⲙⲙⲁϥ
notes.decision: '[That which I am saying]: you yourselves also — that which you have seen [beside your Fath]er is what you do.' Editor restorations accepted; the Johannine pattern (5:19 / 14:12) is here transposed as ethical instruction to the audience.

proposed_terms.rationale: Greek προτομή ('fore-cut, bust, frontispiece, foremost part'). The term needs a translation that distinguishes it from ⲡⲣⲟⲃⲟⲗⲏ ('emanation') and ⲡⲉⲓⲛⲉ ('likeness'). 'Fore-image' preserves the προ- element (forward, foremost projection) and the τομή element (a definite cut form, a bounded representation), while not collapsing into 'emanation' or 'likeness.' Alternatives considered: 'effigy' (too statuary), 'bust' (too anatomical), 'image' (would conflict with ⲉⲓⲕⲱⲛ in L16). Recurs in Manichaean hierarchical descriptions of cosmic figures.

Verbal root meaning 'to shine forth, to dawn, to radiate.' The standard rendering 'Splendor' (German Glanz) flattens this to a static observed quality. The Coptic ⲡⲣⲓⲉ names the active emission of light — what the figure IS doing. 'Radiant' as adjective-substantive preserves the present-active sense. Foundational title of Jesus throughout the Kephalaia.

Lycopolitan term for 'youth, child, young one.' In Manichaean cosmology, this names the third Power called by Jesus the Radiant — sometimes correlated with the Light Maiden/Light Youth figure. Translating literally 'Youth' rather than transliterating preserves the Coptic semantic field.

Idiomatic phrase meaning approximately 'inner depth, recessed interior of mind.' Used both negatively (L5: of the Darkness, ≈ deep-rooted obstinacy) and positively (L17: of the Realm of Greatness, ≈ profound interior). Should be rendered consistently to preserve the bivalent cosmic mirror. Literal preservation of the spatial image follows correspondential principle.
Lycopolitan variant of ⲡⲣ̄ⲣⲟ ('the king'). Should be tagged as such for the lexicon.

translation:
**[Header: ⲗⲉ — page 35; running header: 'Of the Teacher']**

[L1] The First Father has revealed himself. This is the First Father, [L2] the first Power, from whom the three great Powers came forth. [L3] This is the First Father, the first eternal one, the root [L4] of all the lights, from whom the three emanations came [L5] forth. They humbled the Darkness; they crushed his depth of heart; they [L6] appointed a king for themselves alone, and they appointed a king also for the eons.

[L7] The Second Father, who came forth from the First Father, is the Third [L8] Ambassador, the fore-image of the King of the Lights. [L9] He himself also called and sent forth from himself three [L10] Powers. The first is the Pillar of Glory of the Perfect [L11] Man, the one who lifts up beneath all things, the great Pillar [L12] of praise, the great Omophoros who carries all the [L13] omophoroi. The second is Jesus the Radiant who is glorified, [L14] [the one] through whom they give the eternal Life. The third [L15] is the Virgin of Light, the Wisdom who is glorified, who [L16] lifts away the heart of the [arch]ons and Powers in her image (icon), perfecting [L17] the depth of heart of greatness.

[L18] The Third Father, who came forth from the Second Father — [L19] he is Jesus the Radiant who is glorified. He himself also called [L20] three callings according to the likeness of the Second Father. [L21] Now, the first Power that he called is the Mind of Light, [L22] the Father of all the apostles, the first of all the [chu]rches, [L23] whom Jesus established before our likeness in the holy church. [L24] 

The second Power that Jesus call[L25]ed is the gr[eat Ju]dge who gives judgement upon all the souls [L26] of men, with [his] tabernacle established in the air, beneath [...] [L27] [...] the wheel [of the st]ars.

The third Power is [L28] [the] Youth, the great [...] light in his face; twice in [...] [L29] [he is] held on high, whom he established [L30] through the calling [and] the hearing. [He stood] himself beside his [Father], [L31] [the] King of [...] of the s[on...; (those who?)] saw him saying: [L32] [...] "I am the one whom I have seen beside my Father; [L33] [that which I am saying:] you yourselves also — that which you have seen [L34] [beside your Fath]er is what you do."
